title: The inspection capture has no entity, no fields, no screen and no event, its two legacy rule rows belong to other steps of the module, and no requirement maps to FEAT-TRT-15
source: Legacy RWB-E3-015 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md lines 2364 to 2463); FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 A2.15, A2.12.3.1, Screens and Requirements served; TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2 T3.1, T3.2, T4, T6.1, T8; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DIL-18, R-DIL-22, R-RES-12 and R-SET-09; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-TRT-15; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 41 and 42; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01, DP-03, DP-05 and DP-19
section: 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC4; 8 Business rules; 9 State transitions; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.3; 12.5; 12.7; 12.8; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states
description: One combined row for the capture. (1) No source defines an inspection entity, a checklist entity or a bill entity, and TSD S2 T3.1 stops at DF-TRT-033 with no inspection, checklist, photograph or bill field, so the six elements the story writes are the working read of this gap. (2) The FSD field catalog of A2.15 repeats the generic treatment fields and names no inspection field, and the FSD names no screen for the capture: SCR-14, SCR-15 and SCR-16 are the module's screens and the capture is opened on the field app, whose interface no source publishes. (3) TSD S2 T6.1 lists no field-collector role while the FSD names the field collector as the primary actor, so the right the capture needs is carried by the roles that hold U in Treatment and offer. (4) The legacy criteria AC2 and AC3 name R-RES-12 (credit declined, AWAITING_CREDIT_APPROVAL to DECLINED_BY_CREDIT) and R-SET-09 (counter offer below the floor, OFFER_WITH_CUSTOMER_SET to WITH_FCR_OFFICER_SET), which are the credit-decline step of the restructure route and the counter-offer step of the settlement route, not the inspection step whose rule is R-DIL-22; the criteria are kept verbatim and the two rows are evaluated by the sibling slices. (5) Architecture v5 slide 42 gives S2 exactly one event, TreatmentApproved (EV-10), and no source names an event for the inspection completion, so the outcome reaches rwb-case on the case signal. (6) No requirement of the FSD maps to FEAT-TRT-15: the module's REQ-S2-001 to REQ-S2-010 are traced to FEAT-TRT-01 in TSD S2 T8.
evidence: TSD S2 v2 T3.1 ('DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033' and no inspection field) and T6.1 (no field-collector role); FSD S2 v3 A2.15.3.2 (the generic treatment field catalog) and A2.15.2 ('Integration points. Field app, the Workbench document hub'); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-12, R-SET-09, R-DIL-18 and R-DIL-22; legacy RWB-E3-015 section 7 AC2 and AC3; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42 row 10
area: S2 data model, screen and event inventory
owner_role: Business owner of module S2 with the solution architect of rwb-treatment and the rwb-document owner
proposed: Hold the six inspection elements on the treatment row with no new table, carry the checklist, the photographs and the bills as rwb-document references, let the field app reach the service through the gateway-bff composite route with right U of the treatment roles, keep AC2 and AC3 verbatim and hand R-RES-12 and R-SET-09 to the restructure and settlement slices, report the inspection completion on the case signal with no event, and leave the requirement mapping open until a requirement is written for FEAT-TRT-15.

title: The inspection contract identifiers, the element domains, the reference shapes and the fake set are not published for rwb-treatment
source: TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2 T3.1, T3.2 and appendix T-A.1; FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 A2.15.3; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-TRT-15 and the API sheet; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 and R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 and AC6; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.3; 12.7; 12.8; 12.9; 13 Solution plan
description: One combined row for the contract slice. (1) No source publishes a name, a type or a domain for the six inspection elements, and no operation carries them: the service's four operations are the treatment resource, the terms change, the submit and the offer, and the capture has none of its own. (2) No source states whether a checklist reference, a photograph reference and a bill reference are single identifiers or sets, whether the outcome is a code or a text, or which of the six elements a caller cannot leave empty, so the required set is a working read. (3) No source states whether the inspection may publish an event or a case event, and the catalogue gives the service one event type only, so the contract declares that the capture publishes nothing. (4) No source publishes a fake set or a consumer list for the capture, so the fakes of the four consumers are generated from the document itself. (5) The TSD marks the treatment columns as not required at column level, so no source fixes the nullability of an inspection column.
evidence: TSD S2 v2 T3.1 (DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033, no inspection field) and T-A.1 (API-S2-001 to API-S2-004 only); FSD S2 v3 A2.15.3.2; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 APIs sheet (the E3 rows of S2 are the terms change and the submit only); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42 row 10 (one S2 event)
owner_role: Contract owner of rwb-treatment with the rwb-document owner and the field app owner
proposed: Publish the six element names, their domains, their required and optional flags and their absent-until rule in the service contract document at major version 1, with the capture riding on the terms change, no operation and no event of its own, and a generated fake set for the four consumers; treat the domains as the working read of this gap until the document is frozen.
